chunks: The Abbasid Caliph [al-Qa'im bi-Amrillah, Abdullah ibn al-Qadir billah Ahmad] granted him the Chair of Discourse and Instruction (kursi al-kalam wal-ifada),
and this was something they would permit at that time only for the singular, peerless scholar of the age (wahid al-'asr).

key_terms.الْإِفَادَةِ: instruction, scholarly benefit-giving, transmission of knowledge
key_terms.كُرْسِيَّ: chair; the formal seat of scholarly discourse and public instruction
key_terms.وَحِيدِ: the singular, peerless one — denoting the foremost scholar of any given age

ai.seo_question: What honor did the Abbasid Caliph al-Qa'im bi-Amrillah grant to Sheikh al-Tusi (Shaykh al-Ta'ifa)?
ai.summary: The Abbasid Caliph al-Qa'im bi-Amrillah (Abdullah ibn al-Qadir billah Ahmad) conferred upon Sheikh al-Tusi (Shaykh al-Ta'ifa) the prestigious 'Chair of Discourse and Instruction' (kursi al-kalam wal-ifada), an honor at that time reserved exclusively for the unrivalled scholar of the age (wahid al-'asr). This recognition by the Abbasid court — despite the Sunni-Shia sectarian context of Buyid-era Baghdad — stands as a remarkable testament to Sheikh al-Tusi's extraordinary scholarly eminence that transcended confessional boundaries.
